sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento della tensione geopolitica tra USA e Iran, con conseguente spike del prezzo del petrolio. Il VIX è sceso al 17.06, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 15. Il DXY è salito a 100.57, mentre l'S&P 500 è sceso dell'1.21%.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to rising geopolitical tension between the US and Iran, leading to a spike in oil prices. VIX decreased to 17.06 but remains above 15. DXY rose to 100.57, while S&P 500 fell by 1.21%.

market_impact_summary.it: Il mercato azionario è stato colpito dalla tensione geopolitica, con l'S&P 500 che ha perso l'1.21%. Il prezzo del petrolio è sceso sotto i $80 al barile, ma rimane elevato. Il dollaro si è rafforzato rispetto all'euro, con il DXY che ha guadagnato lo 0.48%.
market_impact_summary.en: The stock market was hit by geopolitical tension, with the S&P 500 losing 1.21%. Oil prices fell below $80 per barrel but remain elevated. The dollar strengthened against the euro, with the DXY gaining 0.48%.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.65%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.43%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Sul fronte dei mercati occidentali, nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dell'1.21%, il VIX è sceso del 7.48%, segnale di riduzione dell'avversione al rischio. Il DXY è salito dello 0.48%, mentre l'oro è sceso dell'1.62% a $4288.3/oncia. Il petrolio è in calo del 1.95% a $78 L'US 10Y Yield è salito dello 0.54% al 4.48%. Il BTP 10Y è stabile al 3.82%.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la Fed ha lasciato i tassi invariati nella prima riunione con Kevin Warsh, con proiezioni che indicano un possibile aumento dei tassi. La Banca Centrale delle Filippine ha alzato i tassi per contenere l'inflazione.

Sul fronte macro, nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i sessantaquattromila dollari, con una lieve flessione dell'1,02%. Gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un deflusso di 11,4 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dichiarazioni della Fed riguardo possibili aumenti dei tassi di interesse. 
  Sul fronte delle altcoin, Ethereum scende a mille settecentoquarantacinque dollari, con un calo dell'1,44%. Solana cede lo 0,88% a settantuno virgola ottantuno dollari e BNB perde l'1,75% a cinquecentonovanta virgola ventotto dollari. 
  Il sentiment del mercato, misurato dall'indice Fear & Greed, è a 15, in zona di Extreme Fear, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. 

The Nikkei closed up 1.65%, while Shanghai fell 0.43%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

On the Western markets front, in the previous session, the S&P 500 closed down 1.21%, and the VIX dropped 7.48%, a sign of reduced risk aversion. The DXY rose 0.48%, while gold fell 1.62% to $4,288.3 per ounce. Oil is down 1.95% at $78 The US 10Y Yield rose 0.54% to 4.48%. The 10Y BTP is essentially flat at 3.82%.

On the geopolitical front, the Fed kept interest rates unchanged in its first meeting with Kevin Warsh, with projections indicating a possible rate hike. The Central Bank of the Philippines raised rates to contain inflation.

On the macro front, there are no significant macroeconomic data releases today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above $64,000, with a slight decline of 1.02%. Bitcoin ETFs saw an outflow of $11.4 million. This movement could be influenced by the Fed's recent statements regarding possible interest rate hikes.

On the altcoin front, Ethereum drops to $1,745, down 1.44%. Solana loses 0.88% at $71.81, and BNB falls 1.75% to $590.28

The market sentiment, measured by the Fear & Greed index, is at 15, in the Extreme Fear zone, suggesting caution among investors.

No macroeconomic data in the agenda today. To delve deeper into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Even Hormuz reopening will not resolve Europe’s key energy vulnerability
articles.snippet: Even Hormuz reopening will not resolve Europe’s key energy vulnerability Expert comment thilton.drupal 18 June 2026 Europe remains over reliant on insecure and persistently expensive natural gas. It should focus efforts on reducing demand. European governments, most of which rely on oil and gas imports to fuel their economies, have been nervously watching prices climb and storage levels fall in the weeks since the US-Israeli attack on Iran triggered the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. They could be forgiven for being relieved by this week’s news of a US-Iran framework agreement that promises to enable ships to transit the Strait, through which approximately one-fifth of oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) flowed before the war. articles.snippet: Hungary’s reset with Ukraine is good news for European deterrence Expert comment jon.wallace 17 June 2026 Ending a dispute on minority rights would do more than progress Ukraine’s EU accession talks: it could strengthen the continent’s posture towards Moscow. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Hungary has created the most visible fissure in European Union (EU) support for Kyiv. Former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán dissented early on from the European consensus. And he progressively turned this dissent into political leverage. Budapest slowed sanctions on Russia, contested assistance to Ukraine, obstructed parts of Kyiv’s European path and blurred the moral and strategic line between aggressor and victim. articles.title: Ukraine's fiscal and financial challenges
articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. So far, its authorities have kept monetary and financial stability under control beyond a relatively brief initial episode of turmoil in 2022. What is the broad fiscal equation for Ukraine looking forward, taking into account uncertainties about European funding beyond 2027? Can domestic revenue be raised? articles.title: Embracing carbon uncertainty in portfolio construction
articles.snippet: by Dora Xia, Omar Zulaica We propose a framework for constructing fixed-income portfolios of sovereign bonds that integrates financial and environmental considerations. Central to our approach is the introduction of carbon returns, a concept analogous to financial returns, modeled as random variables to capture the inherent uncertainty of future carbon emissions.

articles.title: Good Medicine Is Combat Power: Clinical Innovation and the Lessons of the Russo-Ukrainian War
articles.snippet: War is a brutal driver of medical innovation. Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has forced clinicians and commanders alike to confront a hard truth: Survival depends not only on tactics and technology, but on the ability to deliver advanced care under fire, evacuate and resuscitate the wounded, and preserve fighting strength despite repeated attacks on healthcare systems.Ukraine’s experience has reshaped combat medicine through necessity, resilience, and improvisation. The central question is no longer whether NATO can observe these lessons, but whether it can build a system bold enough to capture, test, scale, and field them at wartime speed. articles.title: State of Global Oil Inventories Ruins Iran Peace Optimism
articles.snippet: As oil benchmarks crash and Brent slips below $80 per barrel, a growing number of analysts are sounding an alarm: Hormuz may reopen, but oil production in the region would not rebound immediately—and the world’s oil inventories are depleting. Back in May, Carlyle Group’s Jeff Currie warned that by July, parts of the world would face what he dubbed “minimum operational levels” of crude oil supply due to depletion resulting from storage withdrawals to avoid shortages amid the Hormuz crisis.
